content:
Sophie L: sec-bot alert just fired for SSO auth anomalies — rapid MFA pushes across ~28 accounts across multiple tenants. :rotating_light:
Sophie L: seeing impossible-travel flags and rapid IP/UA changes within minutes, looks coordinated.

sec-bot: Alert 6754: sso.anomaly.mfa_push_rate - 28 users - score 0.87 - details: /alerts/6754

Sophie L: sample events:
```
user: user1@example.com, ip: 3.120.45.12 (us-east-1), ua: Chrome/117, event: MFA_PUSH, time: 2026-03-19T22:41:12Z
user: user1@example.com, ip: 51.15.22.99 (fr), ua: curl/7.86, event: SSO_ACCEPT, time: 2026-03-19T22:41:16Z
user: user2@tenantB.com, ip: 13.54.33.7 (us-west-2), ua: iOS, event: MFA_PUSH, time: 2026-03-19T22:42:01Z
```

Jamal K: :eyes: Are these automated push-accepts or user rejects?

Irene P: Checking auth logs now, running query:
`SELECT user, count(*) FROM auth_events WHERE event_type='MFA_PUSH' AND result='SENT' AND timestamp > now() - interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY user ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 50;`
Irene P: initial result shows 26 users with 10-40 pushes each in last 15m.

Ryan M: Do we have concurrent login sessions for these users? Could be device sprawl or token replay.

Sophie L: Yes — multiple active refresh tokens observed for many of them. Suspect credential stuffing + push fatigue.

Jamal K: Immediate containment plan (short):
- revoke active refresh tokens for impacted users
- block suspicious IP ranges at WAF/auth-proxy
- temporarily rate-limit MFA pushes per-user to 1/min
- page oncall and create incident ticket

Irene P: On it. Running quick revoke script:
```
for u in $(cat affected_users.txt); do 
  curl -X POST https://internal-auth/api/v1/tokens/revoke -d "user=$u" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"; 
done
```
Irene P: revoked for first 10 users, continuing.

sec-bot: action: created incident/2026-03-19-ssopush-1, paging oncall-bot

oncall-bot: paging @oncall:security for incident handoff

Ryan M: Also check KMS access logs in case attacker replayed signed sessions or used lifted keys.

Sophie L: KMS logs show no unusual key usages; no anomalous GetPublicKey or Decrypt events in last hour.

Jamal K: Communication draft for support channels:
"Hi — we're investigating an SSO activity spike affecting a small set of users. We've temporarily revoked sessions and rate-limited MFA prompts. If you or your users see unexpected sign-out or new prompts, please let us know. We'll update within 2 hours."

Sophie L: I'll post that to #support-ops and update the status page.

Irene P: Post-incident capture checklist: affected_users.csv, IPs, user agents, push result (accepted/rejected), whether refresh tokens were rotating. Tag audit entries with reason=forced-revoke and incident id.

Ryan M: Postmortem items: add burst detection rule (>5 pushes / 10m), tune impossible-travel thresholds for cross-region within 1m, ensure bulk revoke endpoint is idempotent and fast.

Jamal K: Any blockers for the ACL rollouts?

Sophie L: Need elevated access to auth-proxy to block 3 ranges: 51.15.0.0/16, 3.120.0.0/16, 18.192.0.0/16

Irene P: ACL changes ready, will deploy once Ryan signs off.

Ryan M: Approved, deploy now.

Sophie L: Deployed WAF blocks and rate limits. Monitoring: MFA push rate down ~92% in 10m. :white_check_mark:

Irene P: Will run deeper analysis to determine bot-driven vs credential reuse. Plan tenant outreach for impacted tenants in ~2 hours with list of affected accounts.

Jamal K: Good work. Save logs and evidence to s3://redwood-security/incidents/2026-03-19-ssopush-1 and link in the incident ticket.

Sophie L: Done. Final note: create postmortem ticket, assign action owners for detection tuning and customer comms. I'll AD-hoc update this thread when postmortem exists. Thanks team. :pray:
